declared_skill.name: Verifiable Credential Verification
declared_skill.description: Verifies W3C Verifiable Credentials including Agent Authorization Envelopes with delegation-chain validation.

independent_machine_action.interpretation: MolTrust parsed the exact AG-issued W3C credential through its declared credential-verification operation and attempted issuer-key resolution. It returned a precise unsupported did:key verification-method boundary rather than a schema error or generic probe. The negative verdict is a useful interoperability result: it proves current MolTrust agents cannot independently verify AG passports despite both systems using W3C VC and Ed25519-family primitives.

strict_adjudication.reason: A pre-existing Official A2A specification participant's own hosted trust machine performed its declared W3C credential-verification operation on an exact live Agent Guild passport and returned a specific cryptographic interoperability verdict. Verification failure does not erase the completed AG action; the failure itself is the useful result.

machine_product_signal.observed_gap: A W3C-VC verifier that advertises DID and credential interoperability does not resolve Agent Guild's standard did:key issuer verification method.
machine_product_signal.accepted_direction: Treat verification-method support as a negotiated machine capability. Publish an AGI-1 credential conformance vector that explicitly requires did:key plus eddsa-jcs-2022 support and distinguishes unsupported_method from bad_signature or unknown_issuer.
machine_product_signal.reason: Changing AG's self-sovereign issuer or embedding a credential-supplied trust key would weaken the trust boundary. A portable conformance vector is the correct first adaptation; MolTrust needs resolver support or an explicitly negotiated alternative verification profile.
